axes.comparison: One painted RGBA atlas supplies both lens states. Each textured lamp replaces the two nested flat-color circles in the current Canvas HUD.
The three passive starting lamps retain their one-two-three rhythm on the first start and retry. GO and the PC HUD keep their established cues.
Plum ceramic rims, blue glass and amber light borrow the visual language of the neighboring painted controls and reef set.
Both states have a stable circular outline. The registered alpha masks overlap at 99.90 percent at the half-alpha threshold.
Smoky reflected glass reads off and a creamy amber lens reads lit. Highlights and the inner shade remain within the painted hardware.
In twelve visible comparisons the lowest sampled lit lens center is 237.79 luma and the highest unlit center is 111.0 on the 8-bit scale. Color and brightness both distinguish the states.
Pixel changes are confined to the three original lamp regions with the antialias allowance. The eight adjacent-state and PC pairs are pixel-identical.
The lamps retain their 60-pixel footprint and existing spacing. The original scene, foreground, interaction surfaces and controls are outside the delta.
Each step adds one clear warm light from left to right without labels or reading. Device and child observation remain open.
One 512 by 256 lossless 2D texture, same original state gate and centers, and one texture-region draw per lamp on exact Godot 4.7.2 Mobile and Speedy.

scope: Actual production surfaces at 1280 and 1600. Three initial stages, three retry stages, grid, two GO transitions, and PC split exclusion.
